content: 1. Gemifloxacin and Pantothenic Acid: Gemifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is relevant only when both agents are administered orally. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Probenecid and Gemifloxacin: Probenecid increases the levels of gemifloxacin by reducing its renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 3. Gemifloxacin and Pyridoxine: Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance remains unknown. 4. Gemifloxacin and Pyridoxine (Antidote): Similar to the above, gemifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of pyridoxine (used as an antidote) by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral formulations, and its clinical significance is uncertain. 5. Gemifloxacin and Quazepam: Gemifloxacin increases the levels of quazepam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well established. 6. Quercetin and Gemifloxacin: Quercetin reduces the effects of gemifloxacin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Gemifloxacin and Temazepam: Gemifloxacin increases the levels of temazepam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 8. Gemifloxacin and Thiamine: Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Gemifloxacin and Triazolam: Gemifloxacin increases the levels of triazolam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 10. Gemifloxacin and Acarbose: Gemifloxacin enhances the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Note that quinolone antibiotics, including gemifloxacin, may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Among quinolones, gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 11. Gemifloxacin and Adagrasib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 12. Gemifloxacin and Albuterol: Both agents increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 13. Gemifloxacin and Alfuzosin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Gemifloxacin and Alprazolam: Gemifloxacin increases the levels of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 15. Gemifloxacin and Aluminum Hydroxide: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of gemifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If necessary, separate administration by at least 2 hours. 16. Gemifloxacin and Amifampridine: Gemifloxacin increases the toxicity of amifampridine, potentially leading to seizures. Co-administration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may exacerbate this risk. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Gemifloxacin and Aminolevulinic Acid (Oral): Co-administration increases the toxicity of both agents through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Additionally, avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. 18. Gemifloxacin and Aminolevulinic Acid (Topical): Gemifloxacin increases the phototoxic reaction associated with aminolevulinic acid topical therapy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Gemifloxacin and Amiodarone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 20. Gemifloxacin and Amisulpride: Both agents increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. 21. Gemifloxacin and Amitriptyline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Gemifloxacin and Anagrelide: Both agents increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. Gemifloxacin and Apomorphine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Gemifloxacin and Arformoterol: Both agents increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Gemifloxacin and Aripiprazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Gemifloxacin and Arsenic Trioxide: Both agents increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Gemifloxacin and Artemether: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 28. Gemifloxacin and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both agents increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 29. Gemifloxacin and Asenapine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Gemifloxacin and Asenapine (Transdermal): Both agents increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
